obligation: Processor notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the payment processor (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10 (N44-45-R01)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data, including a fraud alert or common point of purchase notice from the processor, customer reports of fraud after ordering online, or an unexplained change to the online store checkout
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). Clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation
notify: Processor's merchant risk or fraud line (number on the printed contact sheet)

obligation: Card brand compromise procedures, including any forensic investigation (contractual)
citation: Payment brand operating rules, applied through the processor - not law
trigger: Processor or a card brand opens a compromise case
deadline: Per processor and brand instructions (not verified); a PCI Forensic Investigator may be required
notify: Processor; card brands through the processor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow the processor's instructions; brand rules were not verified

trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information, 501.171(1)(a)) of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a credit or debit card number and any required security code, and a user name or email address with a password for an online account (501.171(1)(g)). The store is a covered entity (the definition names sole proprietorships, 501.171(1)(b))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 more days are available only if good cause for delay is given in writing to the Department of Legal Affairs within those 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email to the address in the store's records (501.171(4)(d)); notice must include the date or date range, what was accessed, and how to contact the store (501.171(4)(e))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for card data captured by a fake form

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the store reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep at least 5 years, and provide it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for card data captured with security codes; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more: unlikely, because the store takes about 7 online orders a week and has about 240 online accounts

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store has far fewer than 1,000 online customers

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the store (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent that maintains a system for the store (for example the website builder or the processor) has a breach of security
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the store then owes the notices in 501.171(3) and (4)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Check - online orders are local, but a customer may live in another state part of the year

trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card data or account takeover
deadline: As soon as practical (target within the first day)
notify: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) online report; local police report for the record
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended; a report also supports a law enforcement delay request if needed
No - no cyber coverage; the business owner's policy has no data breach or card compromise coverage (checked 2026-08-14)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC via online form at ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store issues no credit and is not a financial institution under Part 314

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines an incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the store holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
